findings.title: Cache status bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
findings.description: `connectedCalendarsHandler` calls `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()` (`packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-29`). `init()` returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` flag is off, so the mock's new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (`calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-30`, returns `[]`) can never be reached from this caller. With the flag off, existing rows (valid for up to 30 days) still drive the "Last updated" label and the "Delete cached data" option. Fix: `const cacheRepository = await CalendarCache.init(null);`.

findings.title: Unread `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` write runs on every Google push notification
findings.description: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now ends with `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`. Its callers are the Google webhook (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/webhook.ts:46`, invoked on every notification) and the unwatch path (`CalendarService.ts:975`), so every webhook now issues an extra UPDATE. Nothing reads the result: outside this diff's files, no code reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The settings UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. The added `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` selects (`packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:23-27`, `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899-900`) also have no consumer. The cost is modest because `SelectedCalendar` is indexed on `credentialId` (`schema.prisma:891`), but this is dead write traffic and a wider payload on every user load. Remove the call and the selects, or name the consumer.

findings.title: Authorization denial surfaces as a 500
findings.description: The ownership failure throws a plain `Error`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` throws to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a denied request returns a 500 and is reported as a server fault. The sibling handler uses `TRPCError` (`setDestinationCalendar.handler.ts:77`). Use `throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `FORBIDDEN` to match.

findings.title: No tests for the new authorization branch or data paths
findings.description: `deleteCacheHandler` has no test, although the same folder has `setDestinationCalendar.handler.test.ts`. Also untested: `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (`calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-188`, with an existing sibling test file) and the enrichment in `connectedCalendarsHandler`. The ownership test matters most: user B must not be able to delete user A's cache, and an unknown ID must be rejected.

findings.title: Hardcoded `en-US` date format ignores the user's locale
findings.description: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's locale. Other components format with `i18n.language` (e.g. `packages/features/schedules/components/DateOverrideList.tsx:52`). Read `i18n.language` from the same `useLocale()` call this component already makes.

findings.title: Empty 8rem action column left behind for delegated calendars
findings.description: For delegated credentials, `CredentialActionsDropdown` returns `null` (`CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:71-73`), but the wrapper's `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">` is now unconditional. The web `AppListCard` wrapper passes props through to the UI card, which renders `{actions}` unconditionally (`packages/ui/components/app-list-card/AppListCard.tsx:97`). Before this change, the falsy expression rendered nothing. Now an empty 8rem column remains beside those rows. I have not rendered the page, so this is inferred from the markup. Render the wrapper only when the dropdown will show something.

findings.title: Script writes `.env` relative to the working directory
findings.description: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves against the current directory, not the script's location. Run from the repo root, it targets `../.env`, one level above the repo. Run from `scripts/`, it targets the repo root. The root has only `.env.example`, so the first run silently creates `../.env` (lines 62-65). Resolve from the script: `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`.

findings.title: Script exits 0 on failure
findings.description: `cleanup` always ends in `exit 0`. It is also the exit path for a rate-limit hit (line 49) and a failed URL extraction (line 58). A failed run looks successful to any caller or CI step. Have `cleanup` take an exit code (`exit "${1:-0}"`) and pass `1` on the error paths.

findings.title: Migration backfill and header comment
findings.description: `DEFAULT NOW()` gives every existing cache row the deploy timestamp, so "Last updated" will show deploy time for pre-existing entries until they are rewritten. The header block still contains Prisma's generated warning that the column cannot be added without a default, which the SQL below avoids. The timestamp `20250715160635` also sorts before the existing `20250716135157_team_booking_page_cache_feature_flag`. Confirm your deploy tooling applies it correctly on databases that already have the later migration.

findings.title: Stale TODO now contradicts the code
findings.description: The comment says `updatedAt` "doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache table." This PR adds it. Update or remove the comment.

findings.title: Error-row Remove button now honors `disableConnectionModification`
findings.description: The error-row branch previously showed Remove for any non-delegated credential, regardless of `disableConnectionModification`. It now passes the flag through, so Remove disappears when modification is disabled. That may be intended, but it is a behavior change the PR does not mention.

findings.title: `updateManyByCredentialId` accepts a wider type than `updateMany` allows
findings.description: The parameter is `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which includes relation fields. Prisma's `updateMany` input has no relation fields, so a caller could pass one, type-check, and fail at runtime. Type the parameter as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`. The existing `updateById` (line 393) has the same looseness, so this matches the file's convention rather than breaking it.

findings.title: Unrelated changes bundled into the PR
findings.description: The `findMany` change drops a `satisfies` local with no behavior change, and `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` has nothing to do with the calendar cache. Consider splitting both out. The script also uses BSD-only `sed -i ''` (line 68), so it fails on GNU/Linux.

findings.title: All new translation keys exist
findings.description: All 12 keys used by the dropdown and dialogs are present: `remove_app`, `yes_remove_app`, `are_you_sure_you_want_to_remove_this_app`, `app_removed_successfully`, `error_removing_app` (lines 1382-1386), and `cache_status`, `cache_last_updated`, `delete_cached_data`, `cache_deleted_successfully`, `error_deleting_cache`, `confirm_delete_cache`, `yes_delete_cache` (lines 3381-3387).

findings.title: Cache-deletion ownership check is correct
findings.description: The lookup filters on both `id` and `userId`, so a user cannot delete another user's cache. The check itself is sound; the gaps are the error type and the missing test noted above.

findings.title: `cacheUpdatedAt` arrives as a `Date` on the client
findings.description: The tRPC transformer is `superjson`, which preserves `Date` across the wire. The `Date | null` prop type on `CredentialActionsDropdown` is therefore accurate, and `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` receives a real date.
